newsitem.title: IRAN: Frogmen dive into Gulf in Iran's war games.
newsitem.headline: Frogmen dive into Gulf in Iran's war games.

text.p: Iranian frogmen carried out helicopter operations and troops took part in defence against chemical bombardment in war games in the Gulf, the Islamic republic's official news agency IRNA reported on Sunday.

The agency, reporting from Bandar Abbas port overlooking the strategic Strait of Hormuz, said joint navy and revolutionary guard forces also halted a hypothetical enemy advance and penetrated enemy positions in the exercises on Saturday.

Iran launched 10 days of war games in the Gulf and the Gulf of Oman on Thursday involving more than 100 ships including destroyers, gunboats, hovercraft, supply ships and submarines supported by 40 fixed-wing aircraft and helicopters.
IRNA said the purpose of exercise "Piroozi (Victory)-7" was to enhance the combat readiness of the Iranian armed forces.

It quoted a spokesman for the operational commander of the war games and deputy coordinator of Khatam ul-Anbia naval headquarters, Rear-Admiral Ashkbous Danekar, as saying the second stage of the exercises would be launched on Sunday.
Participating units would carry out air defence and frogmen would dive into the Gulf from two helicopters, he said.
Peykan missile-launching vessels would move towards the determined operational zones, he added. Commando units would also carry out underwater defence operations.

Navy Commander Rear Admiral Ali Shamkhani last week condemned the presence of Western navies in the Gulf as "a kind of occupation" but said Iran's exercise "does not challenge anyone and does not signal any tension".
The United States' Fifth Fleet operates in the Gulf. Britain, France and other Western navies are also on patrol.
